lastText: STAVKASVODKAHome19141915191619171918-9MANPOWER-9MUNITIONS-3HOME STABILITYIII.1918Signed at Brest-LitovskThe treaty is signed on 3 March 1918, and the date is New Style because the calendar changed in February along with everything else. It gives up Poland, the Baltic provinces, Finland, Ukraine — territory holding a large part of the Empire's population, coal and grain. It is signed because there is no army left with which to decline it. The front that could not be held in 1915 without shells could not be held in 1918 without men, and the men walked home.Settled recordEast Prussia: entered after the concentration was complete. 1915: the Polish salient was held. August 1915: the Grand Duke retained the supreme command. 1916: the other fronts attacked in support. March 1917: the front commanders advised abdication. June 1917: the offensive was made. Autumn 1914: Galicia was reinforced. The Emperor at headquarters: the question did not arise. The Second Army, August 1914: left to press on. The Carpathians, March 1915: halted in the passes to refit. The Guards, summer 1916: sent at the Stokhod for Kovel. Romania: three divisions sent. The death penalty: not restored. The Kornilov affair: the dismissal refused, and the march collapsed. The order to open talks: carried out. October 1917: the headquarters took no side. The officers of this headquarters disperse toward the Don, toward Siberia, and toward the new Republic's own army. What they do next is not this war.Return to file
